thread:
morgan: Observed weird behavior in go-sdk sample onboarding: prefetch=12, concurrency=3 -> duplicate page processing + token storm. Happens on local dev VM during smoke tests.

lee: Oof. Can you share minimal repro and SDK version?

morgan: go-sdk v1.2.0. Repro steps:
1) checkout sampleapp/go/onboard-prefetch
2) go run ./cmd/warmup --prefetch=12 --concurrency=3
3) run a short auth bounce script that revokes token mid-warmup

Log excerpt:
```
WARN paginator: enqueued=12 workers=3
ERROR auth: refresh failed, retrying
INFO paginator: dispatch page_id=42
INFO paginator: dispatch page_id=42  # duplicate
WARN quota: dropped=6 -> 429
```

sam: Looks like prefetch spawns more iterator tasks than concurrency and on auth-retry the worker count isn't decremented. Go runtime goroutine leak-ish. Node had a similar fix last quarter.

morgan: Workaround I used: set PREFETCH=3 or PREFETCH=0 and add a short sleep in token refresh to avoid tight retry loops. That avoids dupes but hurts warmup speed.

lee: Could be a parity gap. If go-sdk pre-allocates slots and doesn't reclaim on retries that would explain it. Can you attach the small harness? Also which OS/CPU?

morgan: linux x86_64, tiny VM (2 vCPU, 4GB). Gist w/ harness: https://gist.github.com/redwood/ef12gh34

ci-bot: [ci] scheduled job devex/go-warmup-repro #1021

sam: I'll write a unit test that simulates token-refresh error path and asserts prefetch never exceeds concurrency. Assigning to me. Filing issue RDW-4678.

morgan: thanks. adding note to sampleapp README with recommended defaults and the pref/chunk rationale.

sam: will follow up with PR for fix + tests. :thumbsup:
